data.description:
## Problem

MCP tracker `claim` fails on the on-box server with:

```
no certified plan-review attestation (signature: foreign_key; this
environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature)
```

The MCP container is KEY-LESS for op-cert signing.

`rebar._opcert_signing.resolve` picks the op-cert key in this order:

1. a context-local startup binding (`rebar._opcert_binding.current_binding`),
2. the `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` env override,
3. the `<tracker>/.opcert-key` genesis file.

On the live container none of the three yields a key:

- `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` is UNSET,
- `<tracker>/.opcert-key` is ABSENT (tracker is `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`),
- the startup binding, composed by `mcp_server.compose_startup_opcert_binding`
  from `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, is threaded as a
  ContextVar around serving (`rebar._mcp_health.run_mcp`) and is not observed on
  the tool-call path that signs.

`rebar.signing` states the consequence directly: a key-less environment can only
ever report `unsigned` / `foreign_key`.

The Ed25519 key file IS already bind-mounted read-only at
`/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key` by BOTH launch paths (verified present, 411
bytes, in the live container). Only the env var that points at it is missing.

## Scope correction

Both launch paths are affected, not just one:

- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` `mcp:` service — mounts the key, sets
  `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` and `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, but NOT
  `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`. (Line 285 sets it for the `opcert:` service, a
  different service.)
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` blue-green `mcp_run_new` `docker run` — same
  omission. This is the path that actually serves `/mcp`.

`test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service` pins docker-run/compose parity in
the compose-to-run direction, so fixing only the blue-green run would silently
diverge the two. Fix both, keeping compose the source of truth.

## Fix

Set `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key` in the compose `mcp:`
service environment and as a matching `-e` flag on the blue-green `docker run`.
The mount already exists; no new secret, mount, or terraform change is needed.
The env override is thread- and context-independent, so unlike the ContextVar
binding it holds on every tool-call path.

`REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` STAYS. It is load-bearing twice over: it populates
`cfg.identity.signing_key` for authorship signatures, and it is one of the two
required inputs to `compose_startup_opcert_binding` (absent it, the startup
binding is skipped entirely). This change adds a fallback beside it, it does not
replace it.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: the compose `mcp:` service environment sets
  `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH: "/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key"`.
- AC2: the blue-green `docker run` in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` passes
  `-e REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key`.
- AC3: a regression test asserts the blue-green `docker run` command line
  carries that flag with that exact value, and FAILS when the flag is removed
  (mutation-checked).
- AC4: `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` remains set on both paths.
- AC5: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the module-size contract, and the
  complexity ratchet all pass.

## Definition of done

`make lint`, `make typecheck`,
`pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`,
`python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`,
`pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`
all green, and the change is landed through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and
`Verified +1`.

## Non-goals

No terraform. No new secret or mount. No change to the ContextVar startup
binding mechanism (that is a separate hardening question).
data.title: Set REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH for the on-box MCP container
